subject: Hosted to Dedicated — Capacity bridge onboarding agreement and compact cutover plan
messages:
From: Alex Ramos <alex.ramos@clearwater.ai>
To: Hannah Schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood.com>, Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Carla Mendez <procurement@clearwater.ai>
Date: Tue, 12 Jan 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Hosted > Dedicated: sizing validation + cutover timing request

Hi Hannah —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We ran the internal exec sync and the board gave a conditional go: they want a compact acceptance window for moving our 3 critical workloads from the Hosted API into a Dedicated pool.

Top asks from our side so we can sign off quickly:
- A concise validation plan that proves throughput and P95 latency targets on our real traffic profile (particularly chat-sessions with long context).
- A recommended GPU configuration and any quantization tradeoffs.
- A proposed cutover timeline (preferred window: 2/7–2/10) and a clear go/no-go gate by EOD 2/3.

Can your team produce a one-page operational plan + a sizing estimate we can take to procurement? If so, wed like to move forward with a short contract and an onboarding kickoff the week after the cutover.

Carla is on procurement and will need the legal/terms pointer once we have sizing and dates.

Thanks — Alex
Alex Ramos
Head of ML Platforms, Clearwater Labs

Alex — thanks for the clear asks. We can do a compact plan and the sizing estimate. Im proposing the following rapid sequence so Clearwater has the evidence needed for the board and procurement: 

1) By 1/14 — Redwood provides a 1-page "capacity bridge" plan (attached) and a preliminary GPU recommendation (SKU options).
2) 1/18–1/21 — Staged validation in our Reserved sandbox: we mirror a sample of your production traffic (token-limited) and run two throughput profiles (burst and sustained).
3) 1/26 — Joint validation readout with metrics (P50/P95 latency, tokens/sec, failure rate) and an acceptance checklist.
4) Cutover window 2/7–2/10 with a hard go/no-go on 2/3 (we require acceptance results + purchase confirmation).

Were attaching a compact plan (clearwater-compact-plan.pdf) with roles, critical tests, and rollback gates. Ben and Karthik will own the technical validation and will work with your infra team to get the mirrors and credentials. Marissa will be your onboarding lead for the cutover and post-cutover SLAs.

Next steps for you: confirm the acceptance gate (metrics threshold) you need on 1/26 and share a short list of three representative production endpoints for traffic mirroring.

Hannah Schmitt
Director, Solutions — Redwood Inference

> 4) Cutover window 2/7–2/10 with a hard go/no-go on 2/3 (we require acceptance results + purchase confirmation).

Quick technical notes and risks for Alex/procurement: 
- Baseline recommendations (preliminary): 4x A10G per active model slice for long-context chat (context 8k); if Clearwater enables int8 quantization we can fit an additional replica per host but must validate generation quality on the eval set.
- Expected sustained throughput (per 4x A10G): ~1200 tokens/sec aggregate for parallel short requests; P95 ~120–220ms depending on sequence length.
- Mirror/data needs: well require a 48-hour sample trace (anonymized) and a traffic routing rule in your staging VPC so we can run mirrored requests.
- Staging caveat: if your production session mix tilts >40% long-run chains (>1k tokens) we should plan for an extra GPU slice.

I attached a quick XLS with three capacity scenarios (optimistic, baseline, conservative). This is a first-pass — final numbers after the 1/18 sandbox run.

Ben Carter
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
